title: Playing Carnegie Hall and his mother's view of jazz
summary: His first Carnegie Hall concert was 'Spirituals to Swing', which finally won his mother over; she hated jazz because of the Yellow Front and drinking deaths.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What about, what about that famous Carnegie Hall concert?
Well that was my first time ever to play Carnegie Hall and it was the time that
my mother agreed that jazz wasn't all bad, you see.
Oh, in the past she had thought it was?

Yes. You see, when I was going to school, there was a place in Kansas City called 'The Yellow Front'. And everybody went in there with knives and guns, nobody searched you. Every Saturday night somebody got murdered in this place. And it was during that time that my mother thought that jazz was just for low people and she says, she called this place a 'Bucket of Blood'. And she did not want me to play jazz. I don't think it was so much because of the music, but she figures all jazz was not—because at that time look at the young guys that died like Bix Beiderbecke and millions of them from drinking too much, drinking too much. They died at the ages of thirty-six, thirty-eight.
Yes. You see, so my mother didn't want me to get into that kind of life and she never did accept it until I played Carnegie Hall.

No, she was in Kansas. She was in Kansas. And my dad kind of always did like certain people in jazz. But he didn't understand it because as I say, he's a minister, but he was crazy about Fats Waller. He used to always tell me, 'oh, Fats is my man'. But that's the only one. So he never objected to it. And my mother finally came to around where she didn't either.
Well it's really rather funny really because, but still, I suppose Carnegie Hall does have a kind of dur of respectability doesn't it?

Right. My mother came one time to Kansas City to hear me play against Lionel Hampton. I don't remember, I don't know if this was when I was with a band or this was when I was with Jazz at the Philharmonic, but she liked Lionel Hampton's band and she was about 85 years old.

Yes. Maybe a little younger. She might have been eighty. But she always kept up with everything. She kept up with all the baseball teams and she liked this team, didn't like that team. And she liked Lionel's group. I think that's the only
that's the only time she ever saw me play with a group. She never saw me play with Basie.
